kQ5d41kEDQDwVqg1LWVYuK.description: Nancy approached the old house above the lake, not knowing quite what to expect. "The address is right," she told herself.  "but how long has this place been sitting here?  Since the horse and buggy days?" Up the stairs to the huge covered, she tried the door.  And it was open!  She went in and was amazed to see how houses actually looked in 1904.  Paneled walls, beamed ceilings, leaded, bevel edge glass windows, stained glass and the old country kitchen ahead in the next room.  But it was the garret she was most interested in.  She took out her flashlight and made her way slowly up the dark stairs, step by step, until she was at the landing.  The door was open!  Stepping into the room she found the light switch and turned it on.  What presented itself to her eyes was nothing short of a revelation.  Slanted, ceilings, beams, alcoves and furnishings, including a four poster bed straight out of a Victorian fantasy novel. "So this is it.  This is where I'm going to live." $745 later she was, indeed, living there, the most intriguingly magical place she had ever known. G&G, from high above the shores of Lake Union
kQ5d41kEDQDwVqg1LWVYuK.title: Nancy Drew and the Hidden Staircase

1SJVsgHixXsCPdFeNcXLBs.description: I will have a room for rent in the month of September.  This is a large house with 5 bedrooms and 3 bathrooms.  You will be sharing the house with me, a professional gay white dude, 55 years old, retired veteran and full-time gamer.  There is also 1 very friendly Siberian Husky who reside on the property.  I have a full-time job that keeps me very busy. I will not rent this room to anyone who is a hardcore drug user, sex offender, or a felon due to the sensitivity and nature of my occupation.  I will not risk my employment for anyone who falls into the aforementioned categories.  You must be employed if you are to live at this residence.  I will not rent to couples unless the rent is doubled.  Couples forget that electric use and water use rise with more people in the house. I prefer to rent to those who are social and not hide in their rooms until the sun sets.  I live to entertain my friends so they will be over from time to time to play boardgames, D&D, Magic the Gathering, and tabletop miniature games.  I do play on the PS5 and Switch from time to time when not entertaining.  When I am not gaming, I partake in some athletic sports or painting miniatures.  I am very cool, laidback, and a non-drama kind of guy.  I do chill from time to time and binge watch in the living room. Understanding that the times are tough as far as rent is concerned, credit checks, and whatnot, there is no deposit for rent.  Being that I have one dog at my residence, I cannot accept any other pets at this time.  My dog is not cat friendly whatsoever due to a stray cat who constantly torments them. The room is furnished and comes with a huge futon bed, a 70" Smart TV, 4k Blu-ray player, and a PS4.  If you want all of that removed, that could be accommodated.  The room is on the 2nd floor and that would require someone who is ambulatory to climb them.  There is a washer and dryer in the basement for your use.  the kitchen and living room are free to be used.  Respect my property if you use it. If you feel like you are a match, please send me an email and tell me your story.  From there, we can meet and greet, and then show you what I have.

Chinatown, which is located on the southeast side of downtown, is part of the International District, along with Japantown and Little Saigon. It is one of Seattle's eight historic neighborhoods, dating back to the mid-1800s. This popular community is home to some beloved locations, including Seattle's first Chinese restaurant, Tai Tung, which opened in 1935. Other great locations include the New Century Tea Gallery, the historic Panama Hotel, and the Wing Luke Museum. The photo-worthy Chinatown Gate, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, welcomes visitors to Chinatown. Rich with culture and community, Chinatown hosts a variety of events, including the Dragon Fest and the Lunar New Year Festival. Residents gather at the popular Hing Hay Park, which features an elegant pavilion and gate. The park hosts the popular night market, an open-air bazaar, every fall. 44kY3G2tWw833sk4spVKY5.description: Hi all, I’m looking for someone interested in renting a room in a nice craftsman house at the top of Queen Anne. I’ve had good luck with housemates in the past, with many staying good friends afterward. So it probably makes sense to share a bit about me and the other housemate so we can explore if it might be a good fit. I’m a 54 year old male tech worker who is a bit of an extroverted introvert — meaning I enjoy having people over and entertaining, but also enjoy my quiet time. Love cooking, wine and cocktails, as well as movies and good TV shows, and host semi-regular weekly social dinner parties/get togethers to watch with friends. Have a friendly four year old German Shepherd, as well as housesit/care for two a couple of other friends’ dogs on and off. They all have full access to the fenced in yard and house through a dog door, so you’d need to be comfortable with having animals lounging around most of the time. I have one other housemate who currently lives here, and he’ll be available to meet and chat about living here as well. I’m the homeowner, and hope to find someone who enjoys living in the house, is comfortable hanging out in the living room or cooking in the kitchen (if they want), and doesn't feel as though they need to just hide in their room (unless you want quiet time of course). We are both pretty clean, and keep the house in that vein as well with several robot vacuums fighting the ever-present doghair battle. Kitchen is newly remodeled and fully stocked if you enjoy cooking. The house is a block from Queen Anne Avenue and Trader Joes and the new Safeway. The area has easy bus transit and driving access to downtown, and includes a two car driveway (a rarity up here!) Though the ad is for a private bedroom, it's really for living in a full two-story Queen Anne craftsman with finished basement, some off street parking, and some garage storage. I say semi-furnished in the headline because there are a variety of options here — I have a new Queen sized bed and mattress that can be made available, or you can bring your own things. There are two bathrooms (both shared but well maintained), in-house basement laundry and high speed internet (wired/Wifi) with free access to most streaming services is also available (Netflix, HBO, Amazon). The room is currently an office (pictures are from previous tenants), but can easily be freed up within a few days. If interested, there will be a standard rental agreement and one month rent deposit, as well as an applicant paid renter background check (yes, there’s a story there). However, happy to meet first to give you a chance to see the place and see if it makes sense to proceed. Utilities are shared equally across all roommates, with full bill availability/disclosure. For context, Seattle utilities are stupidly expensive, and some bills come every two months — so the total stack tends to jump from low one month to being high the next. A reasonable blended monthly average with three people is probably around $200. Again, the bills are fully transparent and available, no sketchy mystery fees here. Any questions, please drop me a line and thanks for reading! Obligatory tourist details: Queen Anne is known for sweeping vistas, tree lined streets and rolling landscapes. With its iconic coffee houses, the local family friendly business district is home to countless shops, restaurants, and specialty gift stores. You don't have to leave this neighborhood to find some of the city's best dining options with a variety of restaurants that serve Italian, Cuban, Mexican, Vietnamese, Japanese, Thai, French, Seafood, Vegetarian and American dishes.

crPdjKkxXD2QoeCWmpNPuh.description: Tired of cramped rentals, random roommate roulette, and trying to build a real life in a place that feels temporary? This is the opposite. A room is opening in our Sammamish home on 2 acres in the heart of the city. We’re looking for one great fit to join the house. The vibe is clean, quiet, respectful, and high-functioning. The tenant base is also very stable: everyone is on 12-month leases, and renewals are common, so this is not a high-churn roommate setup. Current housemates are working professionals in the software and aerospace industries. The house is quiet, respectful, and very stable. If you’re looking for a calm, well-run home with thoughtful working professionals, this will probably feel like a strong fit. What makes this place different is that it gives you something that is genuinely hard to find on the Eastside: real space, real privacy, and real access to daily life without feeling isolated. You’re in the heart of Sammamish — repeatedly rated one of the best small cities in Washington — but the property itself feels tucked away and deeply Pacific Northwest. It sits on 2 acres, with a seasonal creek, botanical-garden feel, huge windows looking out over a redwood grove, and a steady wildlife show from spring through fall. You can walk to the lake, groceries, banks, restaurants, gyms, and yoga, so this is one of those rare setups where nature and convenience are both right outside your door. The location is strong for commuting too. Highland Sammamish Plaza is within walking distance, and Metropolitan Market is about 2 minutes away. You’re about 5 minutes from the nearest beach and multiple city parks, around 10 minutes to Whole Foods, Costco, Redmond Town Center, Amazon Redmond, and SpaceX, around 15 minutes to Microsoft, T-Mobile, and Costco HQ, and about 20 minutes to Amazon Bellevue and Google Kirkland. The room itself is one of the standout features here. It’s an XL bedroom with a private patio — about 400 square feet for the room itself, plus roughly another 500 square feet of private outdoor patio space. It feels more like a private suite than a typical bedroom rental, with big built-in closets and enough space to actually live in, not just sleep in. It can also come furnished, and the listing photos show the kind of furnished setup available. You also get access to a large shared deck and your own full-size fridge in the kitchen. The house includes a designer kitchen with a JennAir gas range, Thermador convection oven, and Miele dishwasher, plus a high-end Samsung washer, Maytag dryer/steamer, and instant hot water for effectively endless showers. Monthly rent is $1,600 + 1/3 of trailing 12-month average household running costs. That covers your share of utilities (water, sewer, garbage, electricity, gas), high-speed internet, and professional landscaping. This is a strong fit for someone who is clean, considerate, and looking for a calm, quiet, non-party home. It’s a good fit for someone who values peace, privacy, and a beautiful setting — and contributes to that kind of environment. If that sounds like you, reach out and tell us a bit about yourself, what you do, and what kind of living environment you’re looking for. Please include your email in your message. Once a Craigslist ad expires, replies through Craigslist may no longer go through.

Final recommendation will also be dependent on rental, credit & employment history. SECTION 8 APPLICANT CRITERIA: All Section 8 applicants are required to meet the same criteria as stated above, with the exception that the applicant only needs to meet income requirements for their portion of the rent. Recommendations will be made following the above set standards. INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS AND APPLICANTS THAT ARE NEW TO THE COUNTRY: International students will be required to pay a last month’s rent. Proof of current college or university enrollment or current student visa will be required for valid verification. Applicants that are new to the country will be required to pay a First and Increased Deposit. Proof of income source or new job will be required. COSIGNER QUALIFICATION CRITERIA: A cosigner will be APPROVED if all the qualification below is met, if the cosigner does not meet any 1 of the following criteria then the cosigner will not qualify. RENTAL HISTORY: 1 year of valid and verifiable rental or mortgage history with no late payments CREDIT HISTORY: At least 4 accounts in good standing for 1 year with less than $100 in derogatory credit INCOME: 4 times the rental amount of the unit in verifiable, garnishable income GROUNDS FOR DENIAL MAY RESULT FROM THE FOLLOWING ON ALL APPLICANTS: Verified eviction showing on credit report or confirmed with landlord non-Covid related. Rental collection verified on credit report Balance owing to landlord 2 or more late payments and/or NSF checks and/or noise complaints within a 12-month rental period. Derogatory credit history (excluding medical & student loan debt) in excess of $1000 Open (non-discharged) bankruptcy. Unverifiable social security number Falsification of rental application Breaking lease agreement that will result in collection filing Please be advised, a landlord (within the Seattle city limits) is prohibited from requiring disclosure, asking about, rejecting an applicant, or taking adverse action based on any arrest record, conviction record, or criminal history, except sex offender registry information which is the result of an adult criminal conviction – as described in Subsection 14.09.025 A3., 14.09.025 A4., and 14.09.025 A5, and subject to the exclusions and legal requirements in Section 14.09.115. We do not automatically deny applicants based on sex offender registry that is the result of an adult criminal conviction. Rather, consideration is based on the nature of the offense and time passed since the date of final disposition. Supplemental information can be provided to the landlord by the applicant, or produced on behalf of the applicant, with respect to the applicant’s rehabilitation and/or good conduct. Supplemental information may include, but is not limited to: conviction information; certification of rehabilitation; written or oral statements by the applicant, past or present employer(s), current and prior landlord(s), members of the judiciary or law enforcement, parole officer, member of clergy, counselor or therapists, social workers or similar person(s). Rich with culture and community, Chinatown hosts a variety of events, including the Dragon Fest and the Lunar New Year Festival. aoxRJQLCPjuNVNvg6Fmthz.description: We have two bedrooms opening up in our four-bedroom home in North Greenwood, available October 1st and November 1st. Rent is $1,000/month + $125/month for utilities, which includes Wi-Fi. The house has been fully remodeled over the past ten years with high-quality finishes, lots of natural light, and a comfortable, lived-in feel. Both available bedrooms are on the main level and share a bathroom with each other. The other two bedrooms each have their own private bathroom. The available rooms are approximately 10’ x 8’ and can comfortably fit a queen-size bed. Both have closets, multiple functional windows, and privacy with views toward the garden. The house The common areas are already furnished, and the kitchen is large with plenty of storage. Everyone has their own pantry/cupboard space, and there are already plenty of kitchen supplies, so you won’t need to show up with an entire kitchen’s worth of stuff. There’s also a large shared backyard that is maintained by the owner. The property includes a separate backyard cottage where two additional friends live, and we all share the yard. The house is in a quiet residential neighborhood with the Interurban Bike Trail right nearby, making it easy to bike around North Seattle. There’s also easy access to public transportation, including buses and the Northgate Link light rail station. There’s plenty of street parking in the area, and laundry is available in the home. What it’s like living here The four of us currently living between the main house and cottage have been friends for a long time, and we’re excited to welcome some new people into the mix. We’re all 25–28 and work typical 9–5 jobs, so the house tends to be pretty relaxed during the week. We’re a pretty social household—we like to hang out together on weekends, whether that’s watching sports, having people over, going out, or just hanging in the backyard—but we’re also pretty independent during the week and everyone has their own schedules and lives. Between us, our interests include sports, camping, art, and music festivals. Keeping the house clean is important to us. We don’t have a strict chore schedule, but everyone contributes and helps keep the common areas clean and in good shape. Guests are welcome, and we’re currently a no-pets household. A few of us smoke occasionally, but never inside the house, so there are no indoor smoking odors. Overall, we’re looking for people who are friendly, respectful, reasonably clean, and interested in being part of a good household dynamic. Also let us know whether you’re interested in a 6- or 12-month lease. We’re looking forward to meeting some new people and finding a good fit for the house!

4bmw2CNELt4eBvbF5imNcG.description: Live where you matter here at Huntington Place Apartments! Situated in Puyallup, you are right around the corner from Puyallup State Fairgrounds, Downtown Puyallup, as well as South Hill. At this prime location, you are less than a mile away from state route on/off ramps, which will make commuting a breeze! Situated near Route 167 and Route 512, residents find comfort in their direct access to major roadways as well as public transit services. The Washington State Fair is held in Puyallup every September, bringing in more than 1,000,000 visitors to the community each year. Don’t forget to check out some of our famous restaurants in downtown Puyallup featured on ‘Diners, Drive-ins, and Dives,’ such as Crockett’s Public House! Enjoy day-day conveniences such as grocery, coffee, restaurants, shopping, inter-city transit, beautiful parks including bike and walking trails, and nightlife entertainment, this prime location offers it all! We offer a variety of floor plans including: one bedroom/one bathroom apartments, two bedroom/two bathroom apartments', and three bedroom townhomes with two and half baths. Our apartments feature modern interiors such as: Expansive sundrenched windows, efficient stainless-steel appliances, granite countertops, walk-in closets, patio/balconies, and hardwood floors. Our apartment and townhomes were designed with you in mind. Enjoy spacious floor plans with every inch of space masterfully utilized. Our amenities include: An exterior picnic area, exterior playground, all apartments are cable ready, choose the company of your choice to enjoy high-speed internet as well. We are a pet friendly community and accept indoor cats as well as dogs up to 65 pounds; breed and weight restrictions do apply. Fees/deposits are affiliated with having a pet on property. Per apartment, there is a limit of two pets. We have an agility dog park which is an off-leash area for your animals to enjoy! Feel secure where you live, we have security who patrols are property, as well as 24/7 on-site Maintenance for emergencies. We offer all the conveniences you need with an on-line resident portal that includes the option for on-line payments, apartment paperwork, maintenance requests, as well as a resident bulletin board to communicate with other members of our community. We have the below apartment available to move into immediately. Due to our high occupancy and low turnover rates, you do not want to miss your chance to reserve your future home and take advantage of this rare move-in special! We are offering an amazing move-in special! Act now and receive a reduced rental rate for your first lease and up to ONE MONTH of  FREE RENT! **You must sign a 12-month lease to receive this special** Introducing 209/309B: Our two bedroom two bathroom floorplans located on second/third floor featuring 1,065 square feet.   Enjoy patio access, which features an attached storage unit, to enjoy a warm cup of coffee on these cool PNW mornings. Your kitchen features beautiful granite countertops, a deep sink, endless slow-closing cabinetry, and state of the art appliances. The monthly rental rate for 209/309B is on special for: $1,700.00 - $1,800 per month (excluding utilities). If you are interested in the above apartment, please contact us at your earliest convenience. To apply: Please contact us by phone, text, or e-mail. Requirements upon applying are: Your photo identification, application submission, proof of income (one month's worth of current pay stubs), and your holding deposit of $300.00 (due within 24-hours of approval). In person tours are by appointment only. We look forward to assisting you here at Huntington Place!

Tour our beautiful apartment homes, explore our luxury amenities, and discover everything Zella has to offer. Located in vibrant Lower Queen Anne, Zella achieves a peaceful balance between Seattle excitement and the tranquility and harmony of home. This seven-story apartment community brings urban living to a new level thanks to fresh design elements that focus on optimal energy flow. The earthy charcoals of the community’s exterior contrast against brown cedar and red accents to deliver a truly modern aesthetic. Each apartment at Zella is designed to feel both stylish and functional. You’ll enjoy the natural light pouring in through floor-to-ceiling windows , a kitchen that’s as sleek as it is practical with stone countertops, tile backsplash, and stainless-steel appliances , plus the convenience of having your own in-unit laundry . It’s everything you need for comfortable, modern living—right in the heart of Lower Queen Anne. Spend sunny afternoons on the rooftop deck or indoor lounge , fire up the grill in the picnic and BBQ area, or let your pup stretch their legs at the pet park and rinse off at the pet washing station. Need to stay active? The 24-hour fitness center has you covered. For cyclists, there’s a bike repair kiosk and secure bike storage. Plus, package lockers, garage parking , and on-site management make life here easy and convenient. We’re currently offering 6 Weeks Free + a $1,000 Look & Lease bonus when you apply within 24 hours of touring. The Leasing Office is open Monday-Saturday from 9am-6pm. Contact us today or visit zellaseattle.com to schedule a tour and explore available units! Zella Apartments Equal Housing Opportunity

8WKzE2TjmLfjsWbY9QZWJe.description: Discover Luxury Living 🎉 OPEN HOUSE | SATURDAY, OCTOBER 3rd 🎉 Join us for our Open House on Saturday, October 3rd! Tour our beautiful apartment homes, explore our luxury amenities, and discover everything Zella has to offer. With a designated sleeping area, enjoy the comfort and privacy of a bedroom while maintaining an airy, open-concept floor plan. Located in vibrant Lower Queen Anne, Zella achieves a peaceful balance between Seattle excitement and the tranquility and harmony of home. This seven-story apartment community brings urban living to a new level thanks to fresh design elements that focus on optimal energy flow. The earthy charcoals of the community’s exterior contrast against brown cedar and red accents to deliver a truly modern aesthetic. Each apartment at Zella is designed to feel both stylish and functional. You’ll enjoy the natural light pouring in through floor-to-ceiling windows , a kitchen that’s as sleek as it is practical with stone countertops, tile backsplash, and stainless-steel appliances , plus the convenience of having your own in-unit laundry . It’s everything you need for comfortable, modern living—right in the heart of Lower Queen Anne. Spend sunny afternoons on the rooftop deck or indoor lounge , fire up the grill in the picnic and BBQ area, or let your pup stretch their legs at the pet park and rinse off at the pet washing station. Need to stay active? The 24-hour fitness center has you covered. For cyclists, there’s a bike repair kiosk and secure bike storage. Plus, package lockers, garage parking , and on-site management make life here easy and convenient. We’re currently offering 6 Weeks Free + a $1,000 Look & Lease bonus when you apply within 24 hours of touring. The Leasing Office is open Monday-Saturday from 9am-6pm. Chinatown, which is located on the southeast side of downtown, is part of the International District, along with Japantown and Little Saigon. It is one of Seattle's eight historic neighborhoods, dating back to the mid-1800s. This popular community is home to some beloved locations, including Seattle's first Chinese restaurant, Tai Tung, which opened in 1935. Other great locations include the New Century Tea Gallery, the historic Panama Hotel, and the Wing Luke Museum. The photo-worthy Chinatown Gate, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, welcomes visitors to Chinatown. Rich with culture and community, Chinatown hosts a variety of events, including the Dragon Fest and the Lunar New Year Festival. Residents gather at the popular Hing Hay Park, which features an elegant pavilion and gate. The park hosts the popular night market, an open-air bazaar, every fall. 339NdLU9HS6WwcoNxH5Uip.description: Available as early as  October 1st $1,600/month — utilities + high-speed internet included Utilities include: * Water * Gas * Electricity * Trash service * High-speed internet First and last month's rent required. Month-to-month rental but we require a 60 days' notice before moving out. The Space: We are renting out our charming 510 sq ft lower-level "mother-in-law" unit in a quiet Upper Green Lake neighborhood. The unit has: * Private entrance * Private kitchen * Private bathroom * Small closet * Access to a large shared backyard * Shared washer/dryer on site * Abundant street parking * Utilities and high-speed internet included The photos show the space with various furnishings to give you a sense of the layout and size. The unit will be rented unfurnished. The stainless-steel countertop/table and metal shelving shown in the photos can stay if you'd like them; otherwise, we'll remove them. One of the perks of this lower-level tile-floored unit is that it stays wonderfully cool in the summer, which is especially nice during Seattle's increasingly hot summer days. The Backyard: The backyard is a shared space and is a bit of an oasis. It has four mature fruit trees (fig, plum, and apple), a grill, fire pit, cement ping-pong table, and outdoor furniture — all of which you're welcome to enjoy. The yard gets lots of sun, and lawn maintenance is included in the rent. Please Note About Sound: This is a lower-level unit in an older home, so normal household sounds and footsteps from the residence above can be heard at times. The unit is best suited to someone who is comfortable with some degree of normal household noise. We want to be upfront about this so that it's a good fit for everyone! About Location: The house is located just north of Green Lake, approximately a 10-minute walk to both Greenlake and Licton springs Park It's also a very accessible location: * Very quick access to I-5 and 99 (yet insulated from noise) * Multiple public transit options nearby * Light rail access nearby * Abundant street parking directly in front of the house The neighborhood itself is quiet, friendly, and residential. Pets 🐾 Pets are considered on an individual basis, with an additional monthly pet fee. If you have a dog, they would be sharing the backyard with our happy-go-lucky Australian Shepherd, Bodhi. If you have a cat, Bodhi has lived with cats before and is friendly to them, however if your cat goes outdoors may take some introduction for him to learn the cat is 'part of the pack' and not to be chased off the property (which he takes much pride in with squirrels, crows & rabbits). Bodhi isn't much of a barker unless he hears someone unfamiliar entering the house. Otherwise, he's more of a butt-wiggling, gleeful, snorting kind of guy. 😊 About Us: The main house is shared by me, my partner, and Bodhi. We're in our mid-30s — I'm a functional doctor and my partner is a custom stair carpenter. We both work Monday–Friday and keep things pretty mellow during the week. We're also generally fairly low-key on weekends. In the winter, we're often snowboarding on weekends, and in the summer we spend a lot of time camping and exploring. We occasionally have friends over for a dinner or backyard hang on a nice weekend, and maybe an annual or bi-annual birthday celebration, but overall we're pretty quiet and work-focused during the week. Interested? If you're interested, please tell us a little about yourself, what you're looking for in a living situation, profession, and if you feel comfortable to share a social media link. Please mention when you're hoping to move. We'd love to hear a little about you and see if it might be a good fit!
339NdLU9HS6WwcoNxH5Uip.title: MIL/Studio with beautiful back yard

Rental Criteria and Application Disclosure To Apply For Tenancy: 1)	All applicants 18 years or older (or emancipated minors) must have a tour of the interior and exterior of the building either in-person or through a live virtual tour. 2)	After applicant has viewed the unit, they can request an invitation to apply for the unit from landlord/owner. Request can be made in-person, via text, or by email. 3)	Each applicant 18 years or older (or emancipated minor) must complete and submit a rental application through the screening service, Intellirent Solutions, Inc,. and pay the $40 application fee per applicant. If there is more than one applicant in a household, the first applicant will have the option to add additional occupants when completing their application, allowing others in their household to apply. Only a fully completed application packet (which includes all applicant(s) information and documentation and without material omissions or misstatements) will be accepted for review. 4)	The first applicant(s) who submits a complete application and satisfies all published criteria will be offered the unit, as required by Seattle’s First-in-Time Ordinance. 5)	Applicant(s) may request additional time to complete an application for a reasonable accommodation for a disability, a need for language assistance or other meaningful access.  Please contact Sara Weaver by phone or email for this, or any, reasonable accommodation requests. All persons 18 and over (or emancipated minors) intending to rent a property must qualify in each of the below categories, with the exception that the household’s combined income may be used to satisfy the rent to earnings ratio. Credit and Screening Requirements/Criteria - No reported collections within the last six years with the exception of any medical collections, which will not be considered under this collection-history criterion. -No bankruptcy filed or discharged within the last six years. -No unlawful-detainer judgment resulting in eviction within the last six years. With the exception that landlords are prohibited from taking adverse action based on eviction history occurring during or within six months after the end of the civil emergency proclaimed by Mayor Durkan on March 3, 2020, subject to the limited exceptions in SMC 14.09.026. -Credit Score of 700+ (Experian VantageScore) based on the score supplied in the Intellirent Solutions, Inc. screening report. -The household must have verifiable gross monthly income that is 3x the monthly rent. If a rental voucher or subsidy pays part of the rent, the requirement is three times the portion of rent the household is responsible for paying. All lawful sources of income are considered. Verifiable savings also considered (one-twelfth of the verified savings balance will be counted toward the household’s monthly income for screening purposes). Acceptable documentation may include W-2 forms, recent pay statements, employment verification, tax returns, bank statements, benefit statements, rental voucher or other rental assistance documentation, financial aid documentation, or other reliable evidence of income. Applicants beginning new employment may provide a signed employment-offer letter stating compensation and start date that is verifiable. -At least 12 months of verifiable satisfactory rental history is required within the last two years or verifiable mortgage history if applicant was a homeowner. For rental history, all former landlords during the last two years must be included. Rental history must show timely payment, compliance with material lease obligations, proper care of the property and appropriate notice before moving. Unpaid rent, material lease violations and 2 or more late payments may result in denial of application. Mortgage history must show a record of timely payments. Additional Screening Requirements and Criteria Related to Sex Offender Registry We do not request or screen for arrest records, conviction records, or criminal history with the exception of screening for sex offender registry information. Seattle law prohibits rejecting an applicant or taking other adverse action based on arrest records, conviction records, or criminal history, except for permitted sex offense convictions which occurred when the applicant/individual was an adult. Part of our screening includes screening for sex offender registry information. An applicant may be denied tenancy based on sex offender registry information only if a legitimate business reason exists. Our assessment considers the nature and severity of the conviction; the number and types of convictions; the time elapsed since conviction; the individual’s age at conviction; evidence of satisfactory tenancy before or after conviction; and supplemental information regarding rehabilitation, good conduct, or explanations of the registry information. Applicants may provide any supplemental information related to an individual's rehabilitation, good conduct, and facts or explanations regarding their registry information for use in determining if a legitimate business reason exists for denying the applicant/individual. If we deny tenancy or take another adverse action based on sex offender registry information, we will provide written notice identifying the specific registry information that formed the basis for the decision. Only a fully completed application packet (which includes all applicant(s) information and documentation and without material omissions or misstatements) will be accepted for review. 4)	The first applicant(s) who submits a complete application and satisfies all published criteria will be offered the unit, as required by Seattle’s First-in-Time Ordinance. 5)	Applicant(s) may request additional time to complete an application for a reasonable accommodation for a disability, a need for language assistance or other meaningful access.  Please contact Sara Weaver by phone or email for this, or any, reasonable accommodation requests. All persons 18 and over (or emancipated minors) intending to rent a property must qualify in each of the below categories, with the exception that the household’s combined income may be used to satisfy the rent to earnings ratio. Credit and Screening Requirements/Criteria - No reported collections within the last six years with the exception of any medical collections, which will not be considered under this collection-history criterion. -No bankruptcy filed or discharged within the last six years. -No unlawful-detainer judgment resulting in eviction within the last six years. With the exception that landlords are prohibited from taking adverse action based on eviction history occurring during or within six months after the end of the civil emergency proclaimed by Mayor Durkan on March 3, 2020, subject to the limited exceptions in SMC 14.09.026. -Credit Score of 700+ (Experian VantageScore) based on the score supplied in the Intellirent Solutions, Inc. screening report. -The household must have verifiable gross monthly income that is 3x the monthly rent. If a rental voucher or subsidy pays part of the rent, the requirement is three times the portion of rent the household is responsible for paying. All lawful sources of income are considered. Verifiable savings also considered (one-twelfth of the verified savings balance will be counted toward the household’s monthly income for screening purposes). Acceptable documentation may include W-2 forms, recent pay statements, employment verification, tax returns, bank statements, benefit statements, rental voucher or other rental assistance documentation, financial aid documentation, or other reliable evidence of income. Applicants beginning new employment may provide a signed employment-offer letter stating compensation and start date that is verifiable. -At least 12 months of verifiable satisfactory rental history is required within the last two years or verifiable mortgage history if applicant was a homeowner. For rental history, all former landlords during the last two years must be included. Rental history must show timely payment, compliance with material lease obligations, proper care of the property and appropriate notice before moving. Unpaid rent, material lease violations and 2 or more late payments may result in denial of application. Mortgage history must show a record of timely payments. Additional Screening Requirements and Criteria Related to Sex Offender Registry We do not request or screen for arrest records, conviction records, or criminal history with the exception of screening for sex offender registry information. Seattle law prohibits rejecting an applicant or taking other adverse action based on arrest records, conviction records, or criminal history, except for permitted sex offense convictions which occurred when the applicant/individual was an adult. Part of our screening includes screening for sex offender registry information. An applicant may be denied tenancy based on sex offender registry information only if a legitimate business reason exists. Our assessment considers the nature and severity of the conviction; the number and types of convictions; the time elapsed since conviction; the individual’s age at conviction; evidence of satisfactory tenancy before or after conviction; and supplemental information regarding rehabilitation, good conduct, or explanations of the registry information. Applicants may provide any supplemental information related to an individual's rehabilitation, good conduct, and facts or explanations regarding their registry information for use in determining if a legitimate business reason exists for denying the applicant/individual. If we deny tenancy or take another adverse action based on sex offender registry information, we will provide written notice identifying the specific registry information that formed the basis for the decision. General Requirements -All applicants 18 years of age or older (or emancipated minors) must present a valid government issued picture ID. Failure to provide ID results in denial of application. NOTE: WE DO NOT ACCEPT COMPREHENSIVE REUSABLE TENANT SCREENING REPORTS. ONE OWNER IS A LICENSED REAL ESTATE BROKER IN WASHINGTON STATE. The result is a studio that lives larger than most. kK4wtrQAJoqkPfcZeEmWii.description: Perched high above the street in Bremerton's sought-after Manette neighborhood, this home captures sweeping views of the Puget Sound and Olympic Mountains from the main living spaces. Refinished hardwood floors flow through the light-filled living area anchored by a classic brick fireplace. The spacious gourmet kitchen boasts granite countertops, stainless steel appliances, and double corner windows over the sink framing the views.  Retreat to two oversized bedrooms, including a primary suite with French doors opening to an expansive entertainment deck. Three bathrooms offer thoughtful finishes, including a primary bath with a deep jetted soaking tub and separate shower.  The flexible lower-level features warm wood paneling, a freestanding gas stove on a brick hearth, and a custom brick bar—creating an ideal setup for a media room, lounge, or home office.  Outside the fully fenced backyard boasts mature fruit trees and raised garden beds in the front yard. Enjoy a garage with a deep driveway providing lots of parking, and a location minutes from Manette's charming dining, waterfront parks, and the bridge to Downtown Bremerton ferries. Key mechanical updates deliver ultimate peace of mind, including newer roof with ridgeline venting, updated furnace, high-capacity whole-home natural gas generator and more. wtBQPiz1ZRhjMUMAUUdsG5.description: We have two bedrooms opening up in our four-bedroom home in North Greenwood, available October 1st and November 1st. Rent is $600/month + $125/month for utilities, which includes Wi-Fi. The house has been fully remodeled over the past ten years with high-quality finishes, lots of natural light, and a comfortable, lived-in feel. Both available bedrooms are on the main level and share a bathroom with each other. The other two bedrooms each have their own private bathroom. The available rooms are approximately 10’ x 8’ and can comfortably fit a queen-size bed. Both have closets, multiple functional windows, and privacy with views toward the garden. The house The common areas are already furnished, and the kitchen is large with plenty of storage. Everyone has their own pantry/cupboard space, and there are already plenty of kitchen supplies, so you won’t need to show up with an entire kitchen’s worth of stuff. There’s also a large shared backyard that is maintained by the owner. The property includes a separate backyard cottage where two additional friends live, and we all share the yard. The house is in a quiet residential neighborhood with the Interurban Bike Trail right nearby, making it easy to bike around North Seattle. There’s also easy access to public transportation, including buses and the Northgate Link light rail station. There’s plenty of street parking in the area, and laundry is available in the home. What it’s like living here The four of us currently living between the main house and cottage have been friends for a long time, and we’re excited to welcome some new people into the mix. We’re all 25–28 and work typical 9–5 jobs, so the house tends to be pretty relaxed during the week. We’re a pretty social household—we like to hang out together on weekends, whether that’s watching sports, having people over, going out, or just hanging in the backyard—but we’re also pretty independent during the week and everyone has their own schedules and lives. Between us, our interests include sports, camping, art, and music festivals. Keeping the house clean is important to us. We don’t have a strict chore schedule, but everyone contributes and helps keep the common areas clean and in good shape. Guests are welcome, and we’re currently a no-pets household. A few of us smoke occasionally, but never inside the house, so there are no indoor smoking odors. Overall, we’re looking for people who are friendly, respectful, reasonably clean, and interested in being part of a good household dynamic. Logistics * Rent: $600/month * Utilities: $125/month, including Wi-Fi * Available: October 1st & November 1st * Lease: 6 or 12 months * Room size: Approximately 10’ x 8’ * Bathrooms: The two available rooms share a bathroom; the other two bedrooms have private bathrooms * Laundry: In the house * Parking: Plenty of nearby street parking * Pets: No pets * Common areas: Furnished * Kitchen: Fully stocked with plenty of shared supplies and individual pantry/cupboard space * Deposit: $500 refundable security deposit + $100 non-refundable cleaning fee * Application: Application goes through the owner; $40 background check fee If you’re interested, send me a little bit about yourself—what you do, your interests, what you’re looking for in a living situation, and your preferred move-in date. Also let us know whether you’re interested in a 6- or 12-month lease. We’re looking forward to meeting some new people and finding a good fit for the house!

Other great locations include the New Century Tea Gallery, the historic Panama Hotel, and the Wing Luke Museum.
